The whole motivation for this branch was that "before W5-D-9, DEC2BIN was a `Trailing { count }` parser error". A test pinning that the NEW path emits `Token::Ident` is the natural regression guard.
quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-19-phase-5-6-v1-codex.md:1293:docs/audits/2026-05-17-rt-step-1-opus.md:160:The "result depends only on the address/syntactic-shape" rationale is the truth-condition for the dep-suppress: structural-only dependency. But the **runtime** still evaluates Function args eagerly. This is an asymmetry: the dep-walker assumes Function args don't affect the result; the runtime evaluates them anyway. The mismatch creates wasted CPU AND a subtle correctness footgun: if a future reference-aware fn (e.g., a hypothetical `INDIRECT_REF`) was added with Eager contract that genuinely depended on the Function arg's *value*, the dep-suppress walker would NOT track it.
quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-19-phase-5-6-v1-codex.md:1294:docs/audits/2026-05-17-rt-step-1-opus.md:166:1. **Documentation in this commit:** add a comment to `materialize_ref_arg_eager` (or to `is_dep_suppressed_reference_fn`) explicitly noting "eager materializer evaluates Function args; dep walker suppresses recursion for ROW/COLUMN/ROWS/COLUMNS. This is asymmetric — wasted CPU under volatile Function args is the acceptable v1 cost. If a future reference-aware Eager-contract fn genuinely needs Function-arg values to inform its result, REVISIT THIS DECISION (the dep-walker would silently miss the dep)."
quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-19-phase-5-6-v1-codex.md:1295:docs/audits/2026-05-17-rt-step-1-opus.md:223:### MEDIUM-O-3 — `materialize_ref_arg_eager`'s `ExprPlan::AggregateNameRef` arm bypasses `read_range_with_shape`, but a future iterating reference-aware fn would need values.
quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-19-phase-5-6-v1-codex.md:1296:docs/audits/2026-05-17-rt-step-1-opus.md:244:The "populated when the consumer iterates" promise is **not implemented** — there's no path that populates `values`. A future iterating reference-aware fn (e.g., an SUMIFREF-style aggregator) would silently see empty values. The single materializer can't tell which consumer wants values vs not, because `ArgContract` only has Eager / LazyShape — it can't express "Eager with coordinate-only Range" vs "Eager with materialized Range".
quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-19-phase-5-6-v1-codex.md:1297:docs/audits/2026-05-17-rt-step-1-opus.md:248:**Recommendation:** add an assertion or `debug_assert!` in the per-fn impls of ROW/ROWS/COLUMN/COLUMNS — `assert!(values.is_empty())` — so a future-misuse that DOES populate values surfaces loudly. Or, better: drop the `values` field from `RefArg::Range` entirely until the day a consumer needs it. The current shape is mis-specified for v1 (a single empty vec carried around for no reason).

quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-19-phase-5-6-v1-codex.md:1388:docs/audits/2026-05-17-reference-tier-design-codex.md:21:**Detail:** The design correctly states that `ISREF` must not evaluate its argument, but the dispatcher sketch still evaluates every non-`CellRef`/`Range` arg via `eval_scalar_with_cache` and wraps it as `RefArg::Literal`. That means `ISREF(SUM(...))`, `ISREF(1/0)`, volatile functions, and future reference-returning functions are all evaluated even though IronCalc shape-checks the AST directly and does not evaluate (`information.rs:119`). The calcgraph walker also descends all function args (`calcgraph_session.rs:230`), so `ISREF(A1)` and `ISREF(RAND())` would get value/volatile dependencies even though their result is syntactic.

quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-19-phase-5-6-v1-codex.md:1439:docs/audits/2026-05-17-w5-d-2-opus.md:39:Detail: W5-D-2 introduces a new lexer code path (the `if next_is_digit` branch starting at line 552) and a new error condition (the `saw_letter` check at line 569 — pure-digit segments rejected). The implementing commit adds *zero* `#[test]` functions in `lexer::tests` to pin this new behavior. The only happy-path coverage is the e2e tests in `distribution_fns_e2e.rs` (e.g. `t_dist_case_insensitive_lookup_works` which exercises `t.dist.2t`/`t.dist.rt`). A future refactor of `lex_ident_or_ref` could regress the digit-leading branch and the only failures would surface as "T.DIST.2T (unknown function)"-style errors in the e2e suite, not in lexer tests where regressions belong.
quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-19-phase-5-6-v1-codex.md:1441:docs/audits/2026-05-17-w5-d-2-opus.md:52:Severity rationale: MEDIUM. A cross-cutting lexer change without local pin-tests is a regression surface — the engine's lexer module has 441 unit tests for precisely this reason. The fact that the existing trailing-digit test still passes only by coincidence (new branch happens to return the same error char as the old branch) increases the risk: a future maintainer could easily break the digit-leading path without it surfacing in the lexer module. Not HIGH because correctness is verified end-to-end via e2e tests and the implementation itself is correct.

quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-19-phase-5-6-v1-codex.md:1470:docs/audits/2026-05-19-phase-5-2-b-codex.md:3865:docs/audits/2026-05-17-rt-step-2-opus.md:127:**Reachability assessment.** Today, the workbook_runtime has no `delete_sheet` API (grep for `delete_sheet` / `remove_sheet` in workbook_runtime.rs returns 0 production paths). So the deleted-sheet case isn't exercisable from end-user formulas. BUT: any future deletion API will need to either (a) bring this in scope as a regression OR (b) ship with this materializer arm pre-fixed. Also: the WorkbookEnv's `read_cell` returns `Blank` for missing cells in an existing sheet — that's correct and not an error. The error-path is reachable only via the missing-sheet branch today.
quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-19-phase-5-6-v1-codex.md:1472:docs/audits/2026-05-19-phase-5-2-b-codex.md:3886:docs/audits/2026-05-14-phase-4.6-closing-megaudit-sonnet.md:94:Any code that attempts to print a post-bind AST (where `SheetRef::Name` has been resolved to `SheetRef::Id` by the binder) will panic. The rename rewrite round-trip in `workbook_runtime.rs:85–108` correctly uses a pre-bind parse (never binds before printing), so the panic is not triggered in the current happy path. However, this is a latent footgun for any future caller that binds then prints. The design acknowledges this with a "future `print_with_resolver` API" note, but no tracking issue exists. Severity: MEDIUM (no current crash path, but the API is a trap for future contributors).
quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-19-phase-5-6-v1-codex.md:1473:docs/audits/2026-05-19-phase-5-2-b-codex.md:3889:docs/audits/2026-05-14-phase-4.6-closing-megaudit-sonnet.md:297:- The design's `print_with_resolver` API is not implemented (future work, acknowledged).
quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-19-phase-5-6-v1-codex.md:1474:docs/audits/2026-05-19-phase-5-2-b-codex.md:3890:docs/audits/2026-05-14-phase-4.6-closing-megaudit-sonnet.md:322:The rename rewrite round-trip does not trigger this because it never binds before printing. However, the footgun is real: any future code that binds a formula (converting `Name` → `Id`) then attempts to print the AST will panic. Options: (a) implement `print_with_resolver` API that takes a `SheetId → &str` resolver, or (b) add a `#[doc(hidden)]` warning and a prominent comment on `print_sheet_prefix` noting the `Id` panic, and file a tracking issue. For W5-93 close, (b) is acceptable.

Through `OpLog`, there is no public interleaving point between `list.push` and `doc.commit()` because `append` holds `&mut self`: [log.rs](/Users/sanzhar/Documents/Sanzhar/Sanzhar/quantlab/quantlab-quantbook/quantbook-engine/crates/ql-oplog/src/log.rs:76). At raw Loro level, changing peer id during an auto-commit txn triggers a barrier: [loro.rs](/Users/sanzhar/.cargo/registry/src/index.crates.io-1949cf8c6b5b557f/loro-internal-1.12.0/src/loro.rs:187). Pending txn ops keep the peer captured when that txn was created; future txn/appends use the new peer.

Enforce/test uniqueness in the future peer allocation or transport/session registry layer.

This is a latent risk, not a current bug.

quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-19-phase-5-6-v1-codex.md:397:docs/process/audit-protocol.md:312:The split fixes Codex HIGH H1 (bounded ranges silently shrunk under clamp, breaking trailing-blank semantics in lookups). Any future change to `read_range_with_shape` must preserve this branch.
quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-19-phase-5-6-v1-codex.md:398:docs/process/audit-protocol.md:320:The W5-61 wildcard support (`?`, `*`, `~` escape) in SUMIF/COUNTIF/SUMIFS/AVERAGEIF/etc. matches Excel's canon: wildcards target **text cells only**. A `Value::Number(5.0)` cell does NOT match the criteria `"5*"` even though its text representation is `"5"`. If you write a future range-aware function that needs wildcards, route through `Predicate::TextWildcard` (which calls `WildcardPattern::matches`) — do not invent a new path that matches against coerced text representations of numeric cells.
quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-19-phase-5-6-v1-codex.md:399:docs/process/audit-protocol.md:326:`SEARCH` always uses `WildcardPattern::search_in`, even when the needle has no wildcard chars. This is safe because a pattern with only literal chars compiles to a single `Literal` part and behaves identically to a substring search. The pre-W5-61 hand-rolled substring loop was deleted — do not resurrect it. Any future SEARCH change must preserve the wildcard contract (escapes, case-insensitive matching, start_num).

quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-19-phase-5-6-v1-codex.md:454:docs/architecture/2026-05-14-array-formulas-and-spills.md:199:**Why tagged dispatch, not adapter-wrapping:** the alternative ("every register_* shim-wraps the legacy fn into a `FunctionFn`") would require boxing fn pointers (`Box<dyn Fn>`) because a bare `fn` pointer can't capture the wrapped legacy fn pointer. Tagged dispatch keeps fn pointers as plain `fn` values (Copy, no allocation) and pushes the per-tier match into the single eval-site dispatch instead of into per-call adapter calls. Net effect: same single-storage-map win Codex wanted, lower runtime overhead, simpler implementation. Full adapter normalization remains available as a future polish if the eval-site arms grow unwieldy.

quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-19-phase-5-6-v1-codex.md:512:docs/audits/2026-05-17-w5-d-5-opus.md:129:The anchor `0.715_356_905_970_664_3` is statrs's Newton-Raphson output for `t(0.975, df=9) / √10`. True math gives ≈ `0.71531056`. The test comment correctly documents this divergence and the test name `_statrs_self_consistent` reflects the W5-D-3 self-consistency pattern, so this is intentional. The LOW is only a flag: if statrs ever revises its inverse_cdf algorithm (e.g., higher-order Newton or analytic improvement), this anchor will silently shift and the test will fail. There's no test currently asserting "statrs's t(0.975, df=9) ≈ 2.262" as a checkpoint — only the composite `t·σ/√n` value is pinned. A second test pinning just `students_t_with(9.0).inverse_cdf(0.975)` (or referencing the existing T.INV test for this value) would localize a future statrs algorithm change to its source. Minor — current pattern is consistent with W5-D-3.

The W5-56 SEARCH ship may have had these tests; let me note that I greped `crates/ql-functions/src/scalar_fns.rs` for `search_empty\|search.*needle\|empty.*needle.*search` and got zero hits — neither the W5-56 ship nor W5-61 has them.
quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-19-phase-5-6-v1-codex.md:537:docs/audits/2026-05-13-w5-61-megaudit-sonnet.md:93:`crates/ql-functions/src/range_fns.rs:1386-1394`. CONCAT flattens by iterating the `values` Vec in its natural order. The shape comes from `env.read_range_with_shape` at `crates/ql-exec/src/env.rs:144-189`, which populates `for row { for col { out.push(...) } }` — row-major (left-to-right within a row, then row-by-row). For `A1:B2` the order is `A1, B1, A2, B2`. **This matches Excel's CONCAT canon.** But the doc comment on line 1374 just says "row-major order" without explaining what that means for a 2D range. The test `concat_flattens_range` (line 2644) uses a 1×N range, so it doesn't exercise the 2D semantics. A future contributor refactoring `read_range_with_shape` could silently flip this to column-major and only smoke tests on real sheets would catch it.

quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-19-phase-5-6-v1-codex.md:711:docs/audits/2026-05-17-w5-d-11-opus.md:53:4. **No NaN-k pin for either.** While my compiled probe confirmed both kernels reject NaN k via `(0..=1).contains(&NaN) == false` and the engine's `to_number_strict_skip_blank` already maps NaN-bypassing `Value::Number(NaN)` to `#NUM!` upstream, **the test suite does not pin the NaN-k behavior**. Pinning it would harden the implementation against a future refactor that bypasses the `(range).contains` rejection (e.g. if someone re-orders the checks).
quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-19-phase-5-6-v1-codex.md:712:docs/audits/2026-05-17-w5-d-11-opus.md:57:**Severity rationale:** No correctness bug — the behavior is correct under the current code path. But the missing pins mean a future refactor could silently change behavior without test failure. NaN-k in particular: a refactor that moves the bound check below the `pos.floor() as usize` cast (which is `0` for NaN, not a panic in safe-cast Rust) would silently return `sorted[0]` instead of `#NUM!` — a real correctness regression that would slip through.
quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-19-phase-5-6-v1-codex.md:713:docs/audits/2026-05-17-w5-d-11-opus.md:65:**Detail:** Per Codex's documentation review (citing Microsoft TRUNC + QUARTILE.INC docs), Excel truncates a fractional `quart` argument toward zero (TRUNC, not FLOOR). The current implementation uses `n.trunc() as i64` — **correct per Microsoft canon**. But the test suite only pins the positive-fractional case (`quartile_inc_q_truncates_toward_zero`: 2.9 → 2). The negative-fractional case (e.g. `quartile_inc(arr, -0.5)` should return the minimum, NOT `#NUM!`) is NOT pinned. A naive future refactor to `n.floor() as i64` (a plausible misreading of "truncated") would silently change behavior on a sliver of input space without test failure.
quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-19-phase-5-6-v1-codex.md:714:docs/audits/2026-05-17-w5-d-11-opus.md:80:**Severity rationale:** Pure test-coverage gap. The code is correct per Microsoft canon (verified via Codex consultation of Microsoft TRUNC doc). LOW because no behavioral bug — but worth pinning to defend against a future TRUNC→FLOOR refactor.
quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-19-phase-5-6-v1-codex.md:715:docs/audits/2026-05-17-w5-d-11-opus.md:155:**Recommendation:** Leave as-is for W5-D-11 itself (out of scope), but flag for a future polish pass / consolidation.
quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-19-phase-5-6-v1-codex.md:716:docs/audits/2026-05-17-w5-d-11-opus.md:174:**Severity rationale:** Doc precision; no functional impact. Flagged because future maintainers might rely on the "NaN can't reach here" guarantee in a refactor.
quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-19-phase-5-6-v1-codex.md:717:docs/audits/2026-05-17-w5-d-11-opus.md:196:LOW-5 (sort_asc consolidation) is out of scope — defer to a future polish pass.
quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-19-phase-5-6-v1-codex.md:720:docs/audits/2026-05-13-phase-4.6-design-codex-review.txt:23:The current qbook format uses `#[serde(deny_unknown_fields)]` and its documented policy says any future additive field requires a schema bump. Adding `scope` to `NamedEntry` or `NamedTargetWire` while keeping schema v4 means older v4 readers will treat the new file as "supported schema 4" and then fail during TOML deserialization with an unknown field, not with `UnsupportedSchema`. That is exactly the forward-compat hygiene the current schema policy was designed to avoid.
quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-19-phase-5-6-v1-codex.md:721:docs/audits/2026-05-13-phase-4.6-design-codex-review.txt:37:The doc also needs explicit rejection behavior for mixed-sheet two-endpoint ranges such as `Sheet1!A1:Sheet2!B2` and future 3D ranges such as `Sheet1:Sheet3!A1`. Without this, implementers may accidentally create same-sheet fallbacks or silently normalize invalid cross-sheet ranges.
quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-19-phase-5-6-v1-codex.md:722:docs/audits/2026-05-13-phase-4.6-design-codex-review.txt:99:Sheet rename changes sheet-name resolution and printer output, not workbook defined-name lookup. Bumping `name_gen` is coarse and semantically misleading. The design should add a `sheet_gen` or global `semantic_gen` and key PlanCache on it. Rename is rare, so coarse invalidation is fine; the issue is correctness clarity and future maintainability, not performance.
quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-19-phase-5-6-v1-codex.md:724:docs/audits/2026-05-15-phase-4.9-closing-megaudit-codex.md:473:| 13 | **4.9.M** (W5-149, shipped) | Table-driven coverage matrix `(mode × locale × @-presence)` = 30 cells. Each cell specifies a `(mode, locale, input)` triple and the expected canonical (A1+EnUs) output; the driver runs `set_formula(0, 0, 0, input)` and asserts the stored text matches. Modes: A1, R1C1. Locales: EnUs, De, Fr. `@`-presence: none, prefix-cell, prefix-function, inside-arg, prefix-rel-ref. 3 test fns: full-matrix driver, no-duplicate-cells invariant, per-axis dimension counts (pins 2/3/30 so future cell-adds trip the axis sanity test until the doc is updated). Confirms the design § 4.4 canon: stored text is mode + locale invariant; `@` is preserved verbatim. |

quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-19-phase-5-6-v1-codex.md:726:docs/audits/2026-05-15-phase-4.9-closing-megaudit-codex.md:861:./docs/audits/2026-05-14-phase-4.6-closing-megaudit-sonnet.md:94:Any code that attempts to print a post-bind AST (where `SheetRef::Name` has been resolved to `SheetRef::Id` by the binder) will panic. The rename rewrite round-trip in `workbook_runtime.rs:85–108` correctly uses a pre-bind parse (never binds before printing), so the panic is not triggered in the current happy path. However, this is a latent footgun for any future caller that binds then prints. The design acknowledges this with a "future `print_with_resolver` API" note, but no tracking issue exists. Severity: MEDIUM (no current crash path, but the API is a trap for future contributors).
quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-19-phase-5-6-v1-codex.md:727:docs/audits/2026-05-15-phase-4.9-closing-megaudit-codex.md:862:./docs/audits/2026-05-14-phase-4.6-closing-megaudit-sonnet.md:297:- The design's `print_with_resolver` API is not implemented (future work, acknowledged).
quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-19-phase-5-6-v1-codex.md:728:docs/audits/2026-05-15-phase-4.9-closing-megaudit-codex.md:863:./docs/audits/2026-05-14-phase-4.6-closing-megaudit-sonnet.md:322:The rename rewrite round-trip does not trigger this because it never binds before printing. However, the footgun is real: any future code that binds a formula (converting `Name` → `Id`) then attempts to print the AST will panic. Options: (a) implement `print_with_resolver` API that takes a `SheetId → &str` resolver, or (b) add a `#[doc(hidden)]` warning and a prominent comment on `print_sheet_prefix` noting the `Id` panic, and file a tracking issue. For W5-93 close, (b) is acceptable.

quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-19-phase-5-6-v1-codex.md:798:docs/audits/2026-05-14-phase-4.7.D-sonnet-review.md:289:`{1;;3}` would parse as: row 0 = `[1]` succeeds, `Semicolon` advances → row 1 loop begins → `parse_array_cell()` sees `Semicolon` → fallthrough `other => InvalidArrayCellToken { got: "Semicolon" }`. Any future change that perturbs the error-fingerprint (algorithm rotation, sigil string change, etc.) will not be caught.

quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-19-phase-5-6-v1-codex.md:805:docs/audits/2026-05-13-session-final-megaudit-codex.txt:1149:The W5-50 → W5-52 arc is the case study. W5-50 shipped under "GAP-G-01 closed" framing. The `on_clear_formula` clear-path bug shipped silently. quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-19-phase-5-6-v1-codex.md:853:docs/audits/2026-05-14-phase-4.6-closing-megaudit-sonnet.md:94:Any code that attempts to print a post-bind AST (where `SheetRef::Name` has been resolved to `SheetRef::Id` by the binder) will panic. The rename rewrite round-trip in `workbook_runtime.rs:85–108` correctly uses a pre-bind parse (never binds before printing), so the panic is not triggered in the current happy path. However, this is a latent footgun for any future caller that binds then prints. The design acknowledges this with a "future `print_with_resolver` API" note, but no tracking issue exists. Severity: MEDIUM (no current crash path, but the API is a trap for future contributors).
quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-19-phase-5-6-v1-codex.md:854:docs/audits/2026-05-14-phase-4.6-closing-megaudit-sonnet.md:185:`NamedEntry` at `qbook_format.rs:363–377` does NOT have `#[serde(deny_unknown_fields)]`, while `WorkbookEnvelope` (line 248) and `SheetEnvelope` (line 301) both do. This means a v6+ entry with an additional field in a `NamedEntry` object would be silently ignored rather than loudly rejected. The existing v1-v4 / v5 compatibility is unaffected, but the "strict forward-compat" invariant (established in Phase 2A.8 megaudit) is violated for this struct. Severity: LOW (only matters if a future schema version adds a `NamedEntry` field without bumping the version gate).

However, the formula text is persisted via `.qbook` save/load and op-log replay — a stale text will silently carry incorrect references into future phases when named formulas are evaluated. The comment says "today named formulas are deferred" but does not document this as a known gap or file a follow-up issue. Severity: MEDIUM (latent correctness gap, not a current user-visible crash).
quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-19-phase-5-6-v1-codex.md:857:docs/audits/2026-05-14-phase-4.6-closing-megaudit-sonnet.md:297:- The design's `print_with_resolver` API is not implemented (future work, acknowledged).
quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-19-phase-5-6-v1-codex.md:858:docs/audits/2026-05-14-phase-4.6-closing-megaudit-sonnet.md:322:The rename rewrite round-trip does not trigger this because it never binds before printing. However, the footgun is real: any future code that binds a formula (converting `Name` → `Id`) then attempts to print the AST will panic. Options: (a) implement `print_with_resolver` API that takes a `SheetId → &str` resolver, or (b) add a `#[doc(hidden)]` warning and a prominent comment on `print_sheet_prefix` noting the `Id` panic, and file a tracking issue. quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-19-phase-5-6-v1-codex.md:889:docs/audits/2026-05-17-rt-step-3-opus.md:311:1. **Semantic divergence.** Under the design's pseudo-code, `RefArg::Error(_)` would fall through `_ => Value::Error(ErrorValue::NA)` (arity error). The impl returns `Value::Boolean(false)`. These are different user-visible results. Even though the impl path is "unreachable under LazyShape contract", **someone might invoke `isref()` directly from a future test or extension**, and the behavior would silently differ from spec.
quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-19-phase-5-6-v1-codex.md:891:docs/audits/2026-05-17-rt-step-3-opus.md:315:Similarly for ISFORMULA: design says `[_] => Value::Error(ErrorValue::NA)` (arity error). Net behavior matches design, but a future impl reader would have to verify all variants are enumerated.

quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-19-phase-5-6-v1-codex.md:909:docs/audits/2026-05-17-w5-d-1-opus.md:286:(a) **Document explicitly that this path is defensive / dead.** Add a comment above each `match normal_with(...)` saying: "Defensive: Normal::new can fail on NaN mean / Inf-NaN sd, both excluded by upstream sanitize_f64 + the sd > 0 check. The map_err is unreachable but kept to match IronCalc's structure and to fail loudly if a future refactor weakens the upstream guards."
quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-19-phase-5-6-v1-codex.md:910:docs/audits/2026-05-17-w5-d-1-opus.md:288:(b) **Replace with `.expect()`** to assert the invariant explicitly. `let dist = normal_with(mean, sd).expect("upstream sanitize_f64 + sd>0 check guarantees Normal::new succeeds");` makes the invariant load-bearing. If a future refactor breaks it, the panic surfaces in the test suite immediately rather than silently returning `#NUM!` for an unintended path.
quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-19-phase-5-6-v1-codex.md:911:docs/audits/2026-05-17-w5-d-1-opus.md:314:This is correct (Excel: NORM.INV(0, ...) → #NUM!; NORM.INV(1, ...) → #NUM!). But the comment in tests doesn't make explicit why we reject the closed-interval endpoints that statrs allows. The risk is: if a future refactor weakens our pre-check from `<=` / `>=` to `<` / `>` (allowing `p == 0.0` / `p == 1.0` through), the test would then call `dist.inverse_cdf(0.0)` which returns `-Infinity` (not panic actually — let me re-read). statrs's source `if !(0.0..=1.0).contains(&x)` → for `x = 0.0`, `0.0..=1.0` DOES contain 0.0, so no panic. Compute: `erfc_inv(0)` = `+inf`. `mean - (sd * sqrt(2) * inf)` = `-inf`. Then `finite_or_num(-inf) → #NUM!`. So weakening our pre-check to `<` / `>` would still produce `#NUM!` from the finite-check at the end — but for the wrong reason (statrs returning `±inf` rather than us rejecting at the gate). The test would still pass with `Value::Error(ErrorValue::Num)`, but the failure mode would have shifted from "domain check" to "post-hoc Inf-filter."

Not a bug, but the safety net `finite_or_num` exists specifically for this case and is never invoked by any test. Pinning the boundary tells future maintainers that the contract is "finite or #NUM!, no Inf leaks."

quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-19-phase-5-6-v1-codex.md:1028:docs/audits/2026-05-14-phase-4.7.H-codex-review.txt:260:**Why tagged dispatch, not adapter-wrapping:** the alternative ("every register_* shim-wraps the legacy fn into a `FunctionFn`") would require boxing fn pointers (`Box<dyn Fn>`) because a bare `fn` pointer can't capture the wrapped legacy fn pointer. Tagged dispatch keeps fn pointers as plain `fn` values (Copy, no allocation) and pushes the per-tier match into the single eval-site dispatch instead of into per-call adapter calls. Net effect: same single-storage-map win Codex wanted, lower runtime overhead, simpler implementation. Full adapter normalization remains available as a future polish if the eval-site arms grow unwieldy.

quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-19-phase-5-6-v1-codex.md:1052:docs/audits/2026-05-17-rt-step-4-opus.md:454:**Detail:** `text` is a `String`; `Value::Text` wraps `Arc<str>`; `text.into()` converts via the `From<String> for Arc<str>` impl. Allocates a new `Arc<str>` from the `String`. Functionally correct. A future micro-opt: have `formula_text_at` return `Arc<str>` directly (skipping the intermediate `String` allocation), since `Workbook::formula_at` already returns `&Arc<str>`. quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-19-phase-5-6-v1-codex.md:1061:docs/audits/2026-05-14-phase-4.7.H-sonnet-review.md:110:The register loop computes `MAX_ROW + 1` as `u32` — no overflow (MAX_ROW = 1_048_575, u32::MAX = 4_294_967_295) — but it inserts a target entry for a logically out-of-bounds row. The storage layer silently accepts this. This is intentional per design, but a test documenting the behavior (even just asserting the registration succeeds and a target at `MAX_ROW+1` exists in the map) would lock in the "storage is bounds-agnostic" contract so a future reviewer doesn't add accidental defensive clamping.

quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-19-phase-5-6-v1-codex.md:1063:docs/audits/2026-05-17-w5-d-12-opus.md:88:- **Detail:** The engine coerces `Boolean(true)` → 1 → AVERAGE and `Boolean(false)` → 0 → #VALUE!. This matches IronCalc (`cast.rs::cast_to_number` lines 155-161: `CalcResult::Boolean(f) => if f { Ok(1.0) } else { Ok(0.0) }`). But **Excel's own canon rejects Boolean function_num: `=SUBTOTAL(TRUE, A1:A4)` returns #VALUE! in Excel.** The engine matches IronCalc here, not Excel. This is fine, but **the coverage entry does not flag this as an Excel divergence**, while it's pinned by a test that locks in the IronCalc-equivalent behavior. A future Excel-canon enforcement pass would need to break this test.
quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-19-phase-5-6-v1-codex.md:1064:docs/audits/2026-05-17-w5-d-12-opus.md:104:- **Detail:** Both engine `scalar_fns::counta` and IronCalc `subtotal_counta` count errors (engine: `!matches!(v, Value::Blank).count()` includes Error; IronCalc: `String | Number | Boolean | Error => counta += 1`). Behavior matches. **However**, this is NOT pinned by any SUBTOTAL test — the `subtotal_counta_function_num_3` test only covers `[1, "skip", 2, blank, 3]` (no error). A future refactor of `scalar_fns::counta` to skip errors would silently break compatibility with IronCalc + Excel canon (Excel COUNTA does count errors) and the engine-wide aggregate convention. Probe-verified: `SUBTOTAL(3, [1, #DIV/0!, 3]) = ?`. **Not tested** in the new SUBTOTAL block (probe-confirmed = 3.0 — passes through to counta which counts the error).

quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-19-phase-5-6-v1-codex.md:1264:docs/audits/2026-05-18-phase-4-12-megaudit-opus-b.md:169:**Files:** `crates/ql-formula-syntax/tests/p412_defensive_fuzz_probes.rs` — the `try_parse` wrapper uses `panic::catch_unwind` but doesn't isolate to a separate thread. When `deep_function_call_1000` overflows the test-binary main-thread stack, the whole binary aborts — no assertion ever runs, and all subsequent tests in the file silently skip. Engineering note for future fuzz work: every recursion probe must run inside a `thread::Builder::default().spawn(...)` so the overflow is contained.

The whole motivation for this branch was that "before W5-D-9, DEC2BIN was a `Trailing { count }` parser error". A test pinning that the NEW path emits `Token::Ident` is the natural regression guard.
quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-19-phase-5-6-v1-codex.md:1293:docs/audits/2026-05-17-rt-step-1-opus.md:160:The "result depends only on the address/syntactic-shape" rationale is the truth-condition for the dep-suppress: structural-only dependency. But the **runtime** still evaluates Function args eagerly. This is an asymmetry: the dep-walker assumes Function args don't affect the result; the runtime evaluates them anyway. The mismatch creates wasted CPU AND a subtle correctness footgun: if a future reference-aware fn (e.g., a hypothetical `INDIRECT_REF`) was added with Eager contract that genuinely depended on the Function arg's *value*, the dep-suppress walker would NOT track it.
quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-19-phase-5-6-v1-codex.md:1294:docs/audits/2026-05-17-rt-step-1-opus.md:166:1. **Documentation in this commit:** add a comment to `materialize_ref_arg_eager` (or to `is_dep_suppressed_reference_fn`) explicitly noting "eager materializer evaluates Function args; dep walker suppresses recursion for ROW/COLUMN/ROWS/COLUMNS. This is asymmetric — wasted CPU under volatile Function args is the acceptable v1 cost. If a future reference-aware Eager-contract fn genuinely needs Function-arg values to inform its result, REVISIT THIS DECISION (the dep-walker would silently miss the dep)."
quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-19-phase-5-6-v1-codex.md:1295:docs/audits/2026-05-17-rt-step-1-opus.md:223:### MEDIUM-O-3 — `materialize_ref_arg_eager`'s `ExprPlan::AggregateNameRef` arm bypasses `read_range_with_shape`, but a future iterating reference-aware fn would need values.
quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-19-phase-5-6-v1-codex.md:1296:docs/audits/2026-05-17-rt-step-1-opus.md:244:The "populated when the consumer iterates" promise is **not implemented** — there's no path that populates `values`. A future iterating reference-aware fn (e.g., an SUMIFREF-style aggregator) would silently see empty values. The single materializer can't tell which consumer wants values vs not, because `ArgContract` only has Eager / LazyShape — it can't express "Eager with coordinate-only Range" vs "Eager with materialized Range".
quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-19-phase-5-6-v1-codex.md:1297:docs/audits/2026-05-17-rt-step-1-opus.md:248:**Recommendation:** add an assertion or `debug_assert!` in the per-fn impls of ROW/ROWS/COLUMN/COLUMNS — `assert!(values.is_empty())` — so a future-misuse that DOES populate values surfaces loudly. Or, better: drop the `values` field from `RefArg::Range` entirely until the day a consumer needs it. The current shape is mis-specified for v1 (a single empty vec carried around for no reason).

quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-19-phase-5-6-v1-codex.md:1388:docs/audits/2026-05-17-reference-tier-design-codex.md:21:**Detail:** The design correctly states that `ISREF` must not evaluate its argument, but the dispatcher sketch still evaluates every non-`CellRef`/`Range` arg via `eval_scalar_with_cache` and wraps it as `RefArg::Literal`. That means `ISREF(SUM(...))`, `ISREF(1/0)`, volatile functions, and future reference-returning functions are all evaluated even though IronCalc shape-checks the AST directly and does not evaluate (`information.rs:119`). The calcgraph walker also descends all function args (`calcgraph_session.rs:230`), so `ISREF(A1)` and `ISREF(RAND())` would get value/volatile dependencies even though their result is syntactic.

quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-19-phase-5-6-v1-codex.md:1439:docs/audits/2026-05-17-w5-d-2-opus.md:39:Detail: W5-D-2 introduces a new lexer code path (the `if next_is_digit` branch starting at line 552) and a new error condition (the `saw_letter` check at line 569 — pure-digit segments rejected). The implementing commit adds *zero* `#[test]` functions in `lexer::tests` to pin this new behavior. The only happy-path coverage is the e2e tests in `distribution_fns_e2e.rs` (e.g. `t_dist_case_insensitive_lookup_works` which exercises `t.dist.2t`/`t.dist.rt`). A future refactor of `lex_ident_or_ref` could regress the digit-leading branch and the only failures would surface as "T.DIST.2T (unknown function)"-style errors in the e2e suite, not in lexer tests where regressions belong.
quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-19-phase-5-6-v1-codex.md:1441:docs/audits/2026-05-17-w5-d-2-opus.md:52:Severity rationale: MEDIUM. A cross-cutting lexer change without local pin-tests is a regression surface — the engine's lexer module has 441 unit tests for precisely this reason. The fact that the existing trailing-digit test still passes only by coincidence (new branch happens to return the same error char as the old branch) increases the risk: a future maintainer could easily break the digit-leading path without it surfacing in the lexer module. Not HIGH because correctness is verified end-to-end via e2e tests and the implementation itself is correct.

quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-19-phase-5-6-v1-codex.md:1472:docs/audits/2026-05-19-phase-5-2-b-codex.md:3886:docs/audits/2026-05-14-phase-4.6-closing-megaudit-sonnet.md:94:Any code that attempts to print a post-bind AST (where `SheetRef::Name` has been resolved to `SheetRef::Id` by the binder) will panic. The rename rewrite round-trip in `workbook_runtime.rs:85–108` correctly uses a pre-bind parse (never binds before printing), so the panic is not triggered in the current happy path. However, this is a latent footgun for any future caller that binds then prints. The design acknowledges this with a "future `print_with_resolver` API" note, but no tracking issue exists. Severity: MEDIUM (no current crash path, but the API is a trap for future contributors).
quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-19-phase-5-6-v1-codex.md:1473:docs/audits/2026-05-19-phase-5-2-b-codex.md:3889:docs/audits/2026-05-14-phase-4.6-closing-megaudit-sonnet.md:297:- The design's `print_with_resolver` API is not implemented (future work, acknowledged).

However, the footgun is real: any future code that binds a formula (converting `Name` → `Id`) then attempts to print the AST will panic. Options: (a) implement `print_with_resolver` API that takes a `SheetId → &str` resolver, or (b) add a `#[doc(hidden)]` warning and a prominent comment on `print_sheet_prefix` noting the `Id` panic, and file a tracking issue. For W5-93 close, (b) is acceptable.

quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-19-phase-5-6-v1-codex.md:1515:docs/audits/2026-05-19-phase-5-2-b-codex.md:10204:A1. Correct. `loro::LoroDoc::set_peer_id` is only a wrapper over the internal doc setter: [lib.rs](/Users/sanzhar/.cargo/registry/src/index.crates.io-1949cf8c6b5b557f/loro-1.12.0/src/lib.rs:985). The internal state doc says it changes the peer id “for the future txn”: [state.rs](/Users/sanzhar/.cargo/registry/src/index.crates.io-1949cf8c6b5b557f/loro-internal-1.12.0/src/state.rs:491). Existing committed ops are not traversed or rewritten. Transaction creation captures the current peer at [txn.rs](/Users/sanzhar/.cargo/registry/src/index.crates.io-1949cf8c6b5b557f/loro-internal-1.12.0/src/txn.rs:350), and commit writes `ID::new(self.peer, ...)` at [txn.rs](/Users/sanzhar/.cargo/registry/src/index.crates.io-1949cf8c6b5b557f/loro-internal-1.12.0/src/txn.rs:448).
quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-19-phase-5-6-v1-codex.md:1516:docs/audits/2026-05-19-phase-5-2-b-codex.md:10208:A3. Safe after import. Loro `import` runs through `with_barrier`: [loro.rs](/Users/sanzhar/.cargo/registry/src/index.crates.io-1949cf8c6b5b557f/loro-internal-1.12.0/src/loro.rs:568), snapshot decode requires an empty op log: [fast_snapshot.rs](/Users/sanzhar/.cargo/registry/src/index.crates.io-1949cf8c6b5b557f/loro-internal-1.12.0/src/encoding/fast_snapshot.rs:145), and `set_peer_id` then updates only the current/future peer state.
quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-19-phase-5-6-v1-codex.md:1517:docs/audits/2026-05-19-phase-5-2-b-codex.md:10210:A4. Through `OpLog`, there is no public interleaving point between `list.push` and `doc.commit()` because `append` holds `&mut self`: [log.rs](/Users/sanzhar/Documents/Sanzhar/Sanzhar/quantlab/quantlab-quantbook/quantbook-engine/crates/ql-oplog/src/log.rs:76). At raw Loro level, changing peer id during an auto-commit txn triggers a barrier: [loro.rs](/Users/sanzhar/.cargo/registry/src/index.crates.io-1949cf8c6b5b557f/loro-internal-1.12.0/src/loro.rs:187). Pending txn ops keep the peer captured when that txn was created; future txn/appends use the new peer.

I would not add one at this layer: Loro warns this corrupts documents but does not promise a clean detection signal. Enforce/test uniqueness in the future peer allocation or transport/session registry layer.

quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-19-phase-5-6-v1-codex.md:1620:docs/audits/2026-05-13-finalization-merged-plan.md:58:The W5-50 → W5-52 arc is the case study. W5-50 shipped under "GAP-G-01 closed" framing. The `on_clear_formula` clear-path bug shipped silently. quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-19-phase-5-6-v1-codex.md:1622:docs/audits/2026-05-17-phase-4-10-megaudit-opus.md:148:This means: if a future refactor reverts the `"SUBTOTAL"` entry in `is_aggregate_function`, the workspace would still pass `cargo test --workspace`. The invariant test (`is_aggregate_function_lists_only_registered_aggregates`) only checks `lookup_range_aware("SUBTOTAL").is_some()` — that's just a registry-lookup smoke test, not a binder-path test. The HIGH-001 closure has zero test armor.
quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-19-phase-5-6-v1-codex.md:1623:docs/audits/2026-05-17-phase-4-10-megaudit-opus.md:154:The outer SUBTOTAL sums 3 (inner SUBTOTAL result) + 3 = 6. Excel canon: outer would skip nested-SUBTOTAL → return just 3. **This is the documented v1 divergence** (`range_fns.rs:1953-1972` block comment). Fine — documented. But there's also NO test pinning this divergence. A future refactor that accidentally implements nested-skip would break workbook compat with no test failure.
quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-19-phase-5-6-v1-codex.md:1624:docs/audits/2026-05-17-phase-4-10-megaudit-opus.md:179:**Severity rationale:** HIGH. A closure that doesn't test the path it claims to fix is a partial fix. The matrix and master-plan both believe SUBTOTAL is fully shipped. The fix is mechanical (one positive test). The risk is that a future refactor regresses the admission without anyone noticing.
quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-19-phase-5-6-v1-codex.md:1627:docs/audits/2026-05-17-phase-4-10-megaudit-opus.md:288:**Severity rationale:** MEDIUM. The bulk of the corners are correct; the consolidating doc would prevent future maintainers from re-debugging these. Not a code bug, but a structural debt.
quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-19-phase-5-6-v1-codex.md:1628:docs/audits/2026-05-17-phase-4-10-megaudit-opus.md:304:The divergence is documented but not pinned by a test. A future refactor that walks `ExprPlan` to detect nested-SUBTOTAL calls (a legitimate path forward toward Excel parity) would silently change behavior. The test would catch the engine→Excel transition.
quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-19-phase-5-6-v1-codex.md:1629:docs/audits/2026-05-17-phase-4-10-megaudit-opus.md:398:**Detail:** Per CLAUDE.md memory rules, this is acceptable (memory is a snapshot, not a session log). But future sessions reading the memory pointer will get an outdated baseline. The `quantbook_engine_phase4_10_v1_260_shipped.md` file is the authoritative pointer for the current state.
quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-19-phase-5-6-v1-codex.md:1631:docs/audits/2026-05-13-w5-49-50-51-megaudit-sonnet.md:108:The implementation correctly uses `args[0]` as `x` and `args[1]` as `y` (Excel order: `ATAN2(x_num, y_num)`), and the actual call is `y.atan2(x)`. The doc title inverts the argument labels, which is confusing to anyone reading the signature. The function body, the inline comment at line 843, and the test `atan2_basic_quadrants` are all correct. This is a documentation-only error but could mislead a future maintainer.
quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-19-phase-5-6-v1-codex.md:1632:docs/audits/2026-05-13-w5-49-50-51-megaudit-sonnet.md:152:However, as noted in the brief: Phase 3.3 sets `range.sheet = Some(_)` always during binding, so the `unwrap_or(fs)` fallback is currently unreachable. The future cross-sheet case (Phase 4.6) will work correctly if the binder sets `sheet: Some(target_sheet)` for cross-sheet refs. The one risk: if a future binder sets `sheet: None` for cross-sheet refs and relies on context, the supplemental builder would incorrectly scope G's to F's sheet. This is a latent risk, not a current bug.

quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-14-phase-4.7.C-sonnet-review.md:45:**LOW note:** The catchall arm means the compiler will NOT flag if a future `Token` variant is silently swallowed when it should have a dedicated arm. This is an acceptable trade-off at this phase but worth noting as a future maintenance hazard.
quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-14-phase-4.7.C-sonnet-review.md:77:These variants ARE in `ErrorValue::ALL` so they would be recognized by the current code. The `case_insensitive` test covers 3 different sigils (Ref, Value, NA) but not any QB-specific ones. If a future refactor accidentally dropped a QB-specific sigil from `ALL` without updating `sigil()` (which would cause a compile error), or added a typo in `ALL`, there would be no test to catch it.
quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-14-phase-4.7.C-sonnet-review.md:157:This is weaker than `strum::EnumIter` but cheaper to adopt. Alternatively, doc-comment `ALL` with "MUST be updated whenever a variant is added" and add `strum` as a future polish item.
quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-14-phase-4.7.C-sonnet-review.md:172:Five Quantbook-specific error sigils (`#DISCONNECTED!`, `#BINDING!`, `#TIMEOUT!`, `#PERMISSION!`, `#AI_NOT_AVAILABLE_V1`) have no positive lex tests. The code is correct today but the gap would let a future regression in `ErrorValue::ALL` maintenance go undetected.
quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-14-phase-4.7.C-sonnet-review.md:192:There is no assertion that `ErrorValue::ALL` covers all enum variants. A compile-time check via `strum::EnumIter` or a test-time count check would make the lexer's `ALL`-iteration safe against future omission. Suggested pattern shown in §6. This is a LOW because the compile-time exhaustiveness on `sigil()` already catches the most dangerous case.

quantbook-engine/docs/compat/excel-matrix.md:199:| LEN | ✅ | 3 | 4.3 V1 | **DIVERGES from Excel for emoji ZWJ sequences.** Rust counts Unicode scalar values (`.chars().count()`); Excel counts UTF-16 code units (`LENB`-like for non-BMP). For ASCII / BMP-plane text, both match. ZWJ family emoji like `👨‍👩‍👧`: Quantbook = 5, Excel = 8. (Originally anticipated for Phase 4.9 — that phase shipped R1C1+locale-separators+`@`, NOT UTF-16 string semantics. Awaiting a future Phase.) |
quantbook-engine/docs/compat/excel-matrix.md:200:| LEFT / RIGHT / MID | ⚠️ | 9 | 4.3 V2 | W5-56: 1-based positions; UTF-8 char-count (UTF-16 canon deferred to a future Phase, same divergence class as LEN). Negative num_chars → #VALUE!; MID start < 1 → #VALUE!. |
quantbook-engine/docs/compat/excel-matrix.md:201:| UPPER | ⚠️ | 2 | 4.3 V1 | Rust's Unicode-default mapping. **DIVERGES from Excel for German ß** (Quantbook = `SS`, Excel = `ß`) and any other locale-sensitive mapping (Turkish I, Greek final sigma). For ASCII-only text both match. (Originally anticipated for Phase 4.9 locale-aware case — that phase did NOT address case mapping. Awaiting a future Phase.) |
quantbook-engine/docs/compat/excel-matrix.md:202:| LOWER | ⚠️ | 1 | 4.3 V1 | Rust Unicode-default. Same divergence class as UPPER. Awaiting a future Phase. |
quantbook-engine/docs/compat/excel-matrix.md:277:| ISREF | ✅ | 10+11 e2e | RT-V1-01 Step 3 (W5-RT-3) | W5-RT-3: TRUE for cell/range refs (and reference-returning fns in future). Uses `ArgContract::LazyShape` — does NOT evaluate arg, so `ISREF(1/0)` returns FALSE (no #DIV/0!). v1: no reference-returning fns, so `ISREF(SUM(...))` = FALSE always. |

quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-17-w5-d-11-opus.md:53:4. **No NaN-k pin for either.** While my compiled probe confirmed both kernels reject NaN k via `(0..=1).contains(&NaN) == false` and the engine's `to_number_strict_skip_blank` already maps NaN-bypassing `Value::Number(NaN)` to `#NUM!` upstream, **the test suite does not pin the NaN-k behavior**. Pinning it would harden the implementation against a future refactor that bypasses the `(range).contains` rejection (e.g. if someone re-orders the checks).
quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-17-w5-d-11-opus.md:57:**Severity rationale:** No correctness bug — the behavior is correct under the current code path. But the missing pins mean a future refactor could silently change behavior without test failure. NaN-k in particular: a refactor that moves the bound check below the `pos.floor() as usize` cast (which is `0` for NaN, not a panic in safe-cast Rust) would silently return `sorted[0]` instead of `#NUM!` — a real correctness regression that would slip through.
quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-17-w5-d-11-opus.md:65:**Detail:** Per Codex's documentation review (citing Microsoft TRUNC + QUARTILE.INC docs), Excel truncates a fractional `quart` argument toward zero (TRUNC, not FLOOR). The current implementation uses `n.trunc() as i64` — **correct per Microsoft canon**. But the test suite only pins the positive-fractional case (`quartile_inc_q_truncates_toward_zero`: 2.9 → 2). The negative-fractional case (e.g. `quartile_inc(arr, -0.5)` should return the minimum, NOT `#NUM!`) is NOT pinned. A naive future refactor to `n.floor() as i64` (a plausible misreading of "truncated") would silently change behavior on a sliver of input space without test failure.
quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-17-w5-d-11-opus.md:80:**Severity rationale:** Pure test-coverage gap. The code is correct per Microsoft canon (verified via Codex consultation of Microsoft TRUNC doc). LOW because no behavioral bug — but worth pinning to defend against a future TRUNC→FLOOR refactor.

quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-12-megaudit-cycle3.md:65:**Fix**: make `Workbook::put_formula` return `Result<(), InvalidCell>` and validate row/col internally. Or document the invariant + assert at debug-build time. Loader already pre-validates row/col bounds (qbook_format.rs:911-924), so this is defense-in-depth + future-proofing.
quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-12-megaudit-cycle3.md:121:**Agent A finding.** Save path emits `Pending` for `NamedTarget::Constant(Value::Blank)` (via `from_value` returning None → unwrap_or Pending). Load round-trips Pending back to Blank correctly today, but the wire format provides no semantic distinction between "intentionally Blank named constant" and "formula-bearing cell not yet evaluated." Any future change to Pending semantics breaks the named-constant case.

quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-15-phase-4.9-closing-megaudit-codex.md:861:./docs/audits/2026-05-14-phase-4.6-closing-megaudit-sonnet.md:94:Any code that attempts to print a post-bind AST (where `SheetRef::Name` has been resolved to `SheetRef::Id` by the binder) will panic. The rename rewrite round-trip in `workbook_runtime.rs:85–108` correctly uses a pre-bind parse (never binds before printing), so the panic is not triggered in the current happy path. However, this is a latent footgun for any future caller that binds then prints. The design acknowledges this with a "future `print_with_resolver` API" note, but no tracking issue exists. Severity: MEDIUM (no current crash path, but the API is a trap for future contributors).
quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-15-phase-4.9-closing-megaudit-codex.md:862:./docs/audits/2026-05-14-phase-4.6-closing-megaudit-sonnet.md:297:- The design's `print_with_resolver` API is not implemented (future work, acknowledged).
quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-15-phase-4.9-closing-megaudit-codex.md:863:./docs/audits/2026-05-14-phase-4.6-closing-megaudit-sonnet.md:322:The rename rewrite round-trip does not trigger this because it never binds before printing. However, the footgun is real: any future code that binds a formula (converting `Name` → `Id`) then attempts to print the AST will panic. Options: (a) implement `print_with_resolver` API that takes a `SheetId → &str` resolver, or (b) add a `#[doc(hidden)]` warning and a prominent comment on `print_sheet_prefix` noting the `Id` panic, and file a tracking issue. For W5-93 close, (b) is acceptable.

quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-15-phase-4.9-closing-megaudit-codex.md:861:./docs/audits/2026-05-14-phase-4.6-closing-megaudit-sonnet.md:94:Any code that attempts to print a post-bind AST (where `SheetRef::Name` has been resolved to `SheetRef::Id` by the binder) will panic. The rename rewrite round-trip in `workbook_runtime.rs:85–108` correctly uses a pre-bind parse (never binds before printing), so the panic is not triggered in the current happy path. However, this is a latent footgun for any future caller that binds then prints. The design acknowledges this with a "future `print_with_resolver` API" note, but no tracking issue exists. Severity: MEDIUM (no current crash path, but the API is a trap for future contributors).
quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-15-phase-4.9-closing-megaudit-codex.md:862:./docs/audits/2026-05-14-phase-4.6-closing-megaudit-sonnet.md:297:- The design's `print_with_resolver` API is not implemented (future work, acknowledged).
quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-15-phase-4.9-closing-megaudit-codex.md:863:./docs/audits/2026-05-14-phase-4.6-closing-megaudit-sonnet.md:322:The rename rewrite round-trip does not trigger this because it never binds before printing. However, the footgun is real: any future code that binds a formula (converting `Name` → `Id`) then attempts to print the AST will panic. Options: (a) implement `print_with_resolver` API that takes a `SheetId → &str` resolver, or (b) add a `#[doc(hidden)]` warning and a prominent comment on `print_sheet_prefix` noting the `Id` panic, and file a tracking issue. For W5-93 close, (b) is acceptable.

quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-17-w5-d-9-opus.md:57:  Without these, ANY future refactor of `lex_ident_or_ref` risks silently breaking the W5-D-9 path. The whole motivation for this branch was that "before W5-D-9, DEC2BIN was a `Trailing { count }` parser error". A test pinning that the NEW path emits `Token::Ident` is the natural regression guard.
quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-14-phase-4.6-closing-megaudit-sonnet.md:94:Any code that attempts to print a post-bind AST (where `SheetRef::Name` has been resolved to `SheetRef::Id` by the binder) will panic. The rename rewrite round-trip in `workbook_runtime.rs:85–108` correctly uses a pre-bind parse (never binds before printing), so the panic is not triggered in the current happy path. However, this is a latent footgun for any future caller that binds then prints. The design acknowledges this with a "future `print_with_resolver` API" note, but no tracking issue exists. Severity: MEDIUM (no current crash path, but the API is a trap for future contributors).
quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-14-phase-4.6-closing-megaudit-sonnet.md:185:`NamedEntry` at `qbook_format.rs:363–377` does NOT have `#[serde(deny_unknown_fields)]`, while `WorkbookEnvelope` (line 248) and `SheetEnvelope` (line 301) both do. This means a v6+ entry with an additional field in a `NamedEntry` object would be silently ignored rather than loudly rejected. The existing v1-v4 / v5 compatibility is unaffected, but the "strict forward-compat" invariant (established in Phase 2A.8 megaudit) is violated for this struct. Severity: LOW (only matters if a future schema version adds a `NamedEntry` field without bumping the version gate).
quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-14-phase-4.6-closing-megaudit-sonnet.md:241:// (Phase 4.6.D / future): walk NamedTarget::Formula entries for
quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-14-phase-4.6-closing-megaudit-sonnet.md:247:This is currently low-impact because `NamedTarget::Formula` entries are not fully surfaced in the formula-evaluation path (deferred to Phase 3+). However, the formula text is persisted via `.qbook` save/load and op-log replay — a stale text will silently carry incorrect references into future phases when named formulas are evaluated. The comment says "today named formulas are deferred" but does not document this as a known gap or file a follow-up issue. Severity: MEDIUM (latent correctness gap, not a current user-visible crash).
quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-14-phase-4.6-closing-megaudit-sonnet.md:297:- The design's `print_with_resolver` API is not implemented (future work, acknowledged).
quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-14-phase-4.6-closing-megaudit-sonnet.md:322:The rename rewrite round-trip does not trigger this because it never binds before printing. However, the footgun is real: any future code that binds a formula (converting `Name` → `Id`) then attempts to print the AST will panic. Options: (a) implement `print_with_resolver` API that takes a `SheetId → &str` resolver, or (b) add a `#[doc(hidden)]` warning and a prominent comment on `print_sheet_prefix` noting the `Id` panic, and file a tracking issue. For W5-93 close, (b) is acceptable.
quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-14-phase-4.6-closing-megaudit-sonnet.md:379:The four MEDIUM findings are all latent (no current crash or data-loss in the happy path) and address areas where the implementation silently diverges from the design doc or creates footguns for future contributors. The four LOW findings are test-infrastructure and documentation gaps. The overall implementation quality is high: the core parser-workbook decoupling, two-tier name chain, schema v5 save/load, replay reconciliation, and formula-text rewrite on rename are all correctly implemented.

quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-17-reference-tier-design-codex.md:21:**Detail:** The design correctly states that `ISREF` must not evaluate its argument, but the dispatcher sketch still evaluates every non-`CellRef`/`Range` arg via `eval_scalar_with_cache` and wraps it as `RefArg::Literal`. That means `ISREF(SUM(...))`, `ISREF(1/0)`, volatile functions, and future reference-returning functions are all evaluated even though IronCalc shape-checks the AST directly and does not evaluate (`information.rs:119`). The calcgraph walker also descends all function args (`calcgraph_session.rs:230`), so `ISREF(A1)` and `ISREF(RAND())` would get value/volatile dependencies even though their result is syntactic.

quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-17-reference-tier-audit-summary.md:147:| **S2-HIGH-3** | `ROW(SUM(A1:A3))` bind-fails | Document the v1 scope: nested `SUM(A1:A3)`-style literal-range subcalls bind-fail per S1-MED-γ AggregateArg defer. Update `reference_fns.rs` doc-comment + design § 5.6 + excel-matrix Notes to make the scope explicit. The named-range form (`ROW(SUM(NamedRange))`) DOES work and is tested as part of S2-HIGH-1's named-range coverage. |

quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-17-reference-tier-audit-summary.md:234:2. **Walker policy must match each contract.** Step 1.1's address-only walker was designed for Eager fns (ROW/COLUMN/ROWS/COLUMNS). Adding ISREF with LazyShape exposed the asymmetry: the materializer doesn't eval, but the walker walks anyway. **Pattern signal:** each dispatcher contract (Eager / LazyShape / future variants) needs a matched walker policy. Stage future audits to verify both surfaces together.

quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-17-rt-step-4-opus.md:338:If `Workbook::formula_at` returned `Some(Arc::from(""))` (an empty string), `formula_text_at` would return `Some("=")`. FORMULATEXT(A1) would return `Value::Text("=")`. Today the empty-formula state is unreachable: `set_formula` would lex+parse-fail on empty input; `put_formula` raw is internal-test-only in product paths. But `Workbook::put_formula` is `pub`, and a future code path or external integration (e.g., `ql-io` reading a corrupted `.qbook/` formula table) could land an empty string.
quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-17-rt-step-4-opus.md:343:Either add a guard in `formula_text_at` (if `arc.is_empty() { return None; }`), OR add an invariant assertion in `Workbook::put_formula` rejecting empty strings, OR add a defensive test pinning the current behavior so a future change is intentional.
quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-17-rt-step-4-opus.md:418:The ordering is correct, but consider adding a comment block at the head of the match describing the arm-coverage invariant — for future readers / Step 5 work.
quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-17-rt-step-4-opus.md:454:**Detail:** `text` is a `String`; `Value::Text` wraps `Arc<str>`; `text.into()` converts via the `From<String> for Arc<str>` impl. Allocates a new `Arc<str>` from the `String`. Functionally correct. A future micro-opt: have `formula_text_at` return `Arc<str>` directly (skipping the intermediate `String` allocation), since `Workbook::formula_at` already returns `&Arc<str>`. Cost: `format!("={...}")` doesn't compose with Arc cleanly, but a custom builder using `Arc::from(format!(...))` works.
quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-14-phase-4.7.F-sonnet-review.md:57:These correspond exactly to the 12 variants in `crates/ql-formula-syntax/src/ast.rs` (`Expr` enum). The match is exhaustive as a Rust pattern match. If a 13th `Expr` variant were added in a future phase, the compiler would error on `variant_kind` — good. **No gap here.**
quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-14-phase-4.7.F-sonnet-review.md:59:LOW note: `variant_kind` is only invoked on the error path (inside `ArrayCellNotLiteral`). This means the compiler's exhaustiveness check fires at the `variant_kind` definition, not at the call site — a future developer adding `Expr::SomethingNew` will get a compile error in `variant_kind`, not in `bind_with_context`. This is acceptable and consistent.
quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-14-phase-4.7.F-sonnet-review.md:286:**Severity: MEDIUM** — the binder code is correct; the gap is test coverage for the defense-in-depth claim. A future refactor that accidentally narrows `other =>` would not be caught.

quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-14-phase-4.7.F-sonnet-review.md:387:**Severity: LOW** — misleads future developers reading the module docs.

quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-17-w5-d-11-codex.md:29:Detail: The test comment says it verifies that `PERCENTILE` registers to the same function as `PERCENTILE.INC` and `QUARTILE` registers to `QUARTILE.INC`, but the assertions at lines 716-729 only check `lookup_range_aware(...).is_some()`. A future regression that mapped `PERCENTILE` to `percentile_exc` or `QUARTILE` to `quartile_exc` would still pass this e2e test as long as all six names remained registered.

quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-17-w5-d-5-opus.md:129:The anchor `0.715_356_905_970_664_3` is statrs's Newton-Raphson output for `t(0.975, df=9) / √10`. True math gives ≈ `0.71531056`. The test comment correctly documents this divergence and the test name `_statrs_self_consistent` reflects the W5-D-3 self-consistency pattern, so this is intentional. The LOW is only a flag: if statrs ever revises its inverse_cdf algorithm (e.g., higher-order Newton or analytic improvement), this anchor will silently shift and the test will fail. There's no test currently asserting "statrs's t(0.975, df=9) ≈ 2.262" as a checkpoint — only the composite `t·σ/√n` value is pinned. A second test pinning just `students_t_with(9.0).inverse_cdf(0.975)` (or referencing the existing T.INV test for this value) would localize a future statrs algorithm change to its source. Minor — current pattern is consistent with W5-D-3.

quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-14-phase-4.7.C-sonnet-review.md:45:**LOW note:** The catchall arm means the compiler will NOT flag if a future `Token` variant is silently swallowed when it should have a dedicated arm. This is an acceptable trade-off at this phase but worth noting as a future maintenance hazard.
quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-14-phase-4.7.C-sonnet-review.md:77:These variants ARE in `ErrorValue::ALL` so they would be recognized by the current code. The `case_insensitive` test covers 3 different sigils (Ref, Value, NA) but not any QB-specific ones. If a future refactor accidentally dropped a QB-specific sigil from `ALL` without updating `sigil()` (which would cause a compile error), or added a typo in `ALL`, there would be no test to catch it.
quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-14-phase-4.7.C-sonnet-review.md:157:This is weaker than `strum::EnumIter` but cheaper to adopt. Alternatively, doc-comment `ALL` with "MUST be updated whenever a variant is added" and add `strum` as a future polish item.
quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-14-phase-4.7.C-sonnet-review.md:172:Five Quantbook-specific error sigils (`#DISCONNECTED!`, `#BINDING!`, `#TIMEOUT!`, `#PERMISSION!`, `#AI_NOT_AVAILABLE_V1`) have no positive lex tests. The code is correct today but the gap would let a future regression in `ErrorValue::ALL` maintenance go undetected.
quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-14-phase-4.7.C-sonnet-review.md:192:There is no assertion that `ErrorValue::ALL` covers all enum variants. A compile-time check via `strum::EnumIter` or a test-time count check would make the lexer's `ALL`-iteration safe against future omission. Suggested pattern shown in §6. This is a LOW because the compile-time exhaustiveness on `sigil()` already catches the most dangerous case.
quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-17-w5-d-6-opus.md:151:IronCalc uses the same two-pass approach, so this is parity-by-design and not a defect. Worth noting only because future ULP-sensitive callers may want to swap in a higher-precision kernel; the `compute_covariance` interface is well-suited for that future refactor.

quantbook-engine/docs/compat/excel-matrix.md:199:| LEN | ✅ | 3 | 4.3 V1 | **DIVERGES from Excel for emoji ZWJ sequences.** Rust counts Unicode scalar values (`.chars().count()`); Excel counts UTF-16 code units (`LENB`-like for non-BMP). For ASCII / BMP-plane text, both match. ZWJ family emoji like `👨‍👩‍👧`: Quantbook = 5, Excel = 8. (Originally anticipated for Phase 4.9 — that phase shipped R1C1+locale-separators+`@`, NOT UTF-16 string semantics. Awaiting a future Phase.) |
quantbook-engine/docs/compat/excel-matrix.md:200:| LEFT / RIGHT / MID | ⚠️ | 9 | 4.3 V2 | W5-56: 1-based positions; UTF-8 char-count (UTF-16 canon deferred to a future Phase, same divergence class as LEN). Negative num_chars → #VALUE!; MID start < 1 → #VALUE!. |
quantbook-engine/docs/compat/excel-matrix.md:201:| UPPER | ⚠️ | 2 | 4.3 V1 | Rust's Unicode-default mapping. **DIVERGES from Excel for German ß** (Quantbook = `SS`, Excel = `ß`) and any other locale-sensitive mapping (Turkish I, Greek final sigma). For ASCII-only text both match. (Originally anticipated for Phase 4.9 locale-aware case — that phase did NOT address case mapping. Awaiting a future Phase.) |
quantbook-engine/docs/compat/excel-matrix.md:202:| LOWER | ⚠️ | 1 | 4.3 V1 | Rust Unicode-default. Same divergence class as UPPER. Awaiting a future Phase. |
quantbook-engine/docs/compat/excel-matrix.md:277:| ISREF | ✅ | 10+11 e2e | RT-V1-01 Step 3 (W5-RT-3) | W5-RT-3: TRUE for cell/range refs (and reference-returning fns in future). Uses `ArgContract::LazyShape` — does NOT evaluate arg, so `ISREF(1/0)` returns FALSE (no #DIV/0!). v1: no reference-returning fns, so `ISREF(SUM(...))` = FALSE always. |

quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-15-phase-4.8-closing-megaudit-codex.md:339:./docs/audits/2026-05-13-phase-4.6-design-codex-review.txt:23:The current qbook format uses `#[serde(deny_unknown_fields)]` and its documented policy says any future additive field requires a schema bump. Adding `scope` to `NamedEntry` or `NamedTargetWire` while keeping schema v4 means older v4 readers will treat the new file as "supported schema 4" and then fail during TOML deserialization with an unknown field, not with `UnsupportedSchema`. That is exactly the forward-compat hygiene the current schema policy was designed to avoid.

This means a v6+ entry with an additional field in a `NamedEntry` object would be silently ignored rather than loudly rejected. The existing v1-v4 / v5 compatibility is unaffected, but the "strict forward-compat" invariant (established in Phase 2A.8 megaudit) is violated for this struct. Severity: LOW (only matters if a future schema version adds a `NamedEntry` field without bumping the version gate).

quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-17-w5-d-12-opus.md:88:- **Detail:** The engine coerces `Boolean(true)` → 1 → AVERAGE and `Boolean(false)` → 0 → #VALUE!. This matches IronCalc (`cast.rs::cast_to_number` lines 155-161: `CalcResult::Boolean(f) => if f { Ok(1.0) } else { Ok(0.0) }`). But **Excel's own canon rejects Boolean function_num: `=SUBTOTAL(TRUE, A1:A4)` returns #VALUE! in Excel.** The engine matches IronCalc here, not Excel. This is fine, but **the coverage entry does not flag this as an Excel divergence**, while it's pinned by a test that locks in the IronCalc-equivalent behavior. A future Excel-canon enforcement pass would need to break this test.
quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-17-w5-d-12-opus.md:104:- **Detail:** Both engine `scalar_fns::counta` and IronCalc `subtotal_counta` count errors (engine: `!matches!(v, Value::Blank).count()` includes Error; IronCalc: `String | Number | Boolean | Error => counta += 1`). Behavior matches. **However**, this is NOT pinned by any SUBTOTAL test — the `subtotal_counta_function_num_3` test only covers `[1, "skip", 2, blank, 3]` (no error). A future refactor of `scalar_fns::counta` to skip errors would silently break compatibility with IronCalc + Excel canon (Excel COUNTA does count errors) and the engine-wide aggregate convention. Probe-verified: `SUBTOTAL(3, [1, #DIV/0!, 3]) = ?`. **Not tested** in the new SUBTOTAL block (probe-confirmed = 3.0 — passes through to counta which counts the error).

quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-18-phase-4-12-megaudit-opus-b.md:89:- The op-log layer's design comment at `op.rs:142` explicitly says "Nested BatchCommits are permitted by the schema but produced nowhere in production; replay handles them via recursion." That's an *intentional* defensive gap — relying on serde_json's *default* recursion limit to bound stack depth is an implicit dependency. Two ways this fails today or in the future:
quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-18-phase-4-12-megaudit-opus-b.md:143:**Why M:** Defensive surface is acceptable today (every malformed snapshot returns `OpLogError::Loro(...)` rather than panicking). The note is for future hardening: if Loro adds checksumming or zstd payload framing changes upstream, the wrapper here is a thin pass-through and might miss class-shifting changes (e.g. format magic-byte added later — the wrapper doesn't sniff anything itself). Add an explicit min-bytes/magic-bytes pre-check at the wrapper layer to make the failure mode independent of Loro internals. Not a bug right now; defensive depth.
quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-18-phase-4-12-megaudit-opus-b.md:169:**Files:** `crates/ql-formula-syntax/tests/p412_defensive_fuzz_probes.rs` — the `try_parse` wrapper uses `panic::catch_unwind` but doesn't isolate to a separate thread. When `deep_function_call_1000` overflows the test-binary main-thread stack, the whole binary aborts — no assertion ever runs, and all subsequent tests in the file silently skip. Engineering note for future fuzz work: every recursion probe must run inside a `thread::Builder::default().spawn(...)` so the overflow is contained.

quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-14-phase-4.7.H-sonnet-review.md:110:The register loop computes `MAX_ROW + 1` as `u32` — no overflow (MAX_ROW = 1_048_575, u32::MAX = 4_294_967_295) — but it inserts a target entry for a logically out-of-bounds row. The storage layer silently accepts this. This is intentional per design, but a test documenting the behavior (even just asserting the registration succeeds and a target at `MAX_ROW+1` exists in the map) would lock in the "storage is bounds-agnostic" contract so a future reviewer doesn't add accidental defensive clamping.

quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-18-phase-4-11-architecture-codex.md:98:There are two valid product futures.
quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-18-phase-4-11-architecture-codex.md:102:If Excel remains a live interchange format with repeated back-and-forth edits, fidelity loss compounds. Dropping a data validation or conditional format on the first export is not a cosmetic bug; it permanently damages a workbook another collaborator may still own in Excel. This future requires update-original export, opaque package preservation, and strict unsupported-feature policy. It also means the importer should store an `XlsxPreservation` handle or original package fingerprint for workbooks that came from XLSX.
quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-18-phase-4-11-architecture-codex.md:129:| Roll-own reader first | Long runway before common workbooks import; reimplements shared strings, formulas, worksheet edge cases, styles, rels. | Medium | High | Keep a narrow OOXML scanner now. Define backend traits so a future roll-own grid reader can replace calamine if needed. |

quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-17-rt-step-3-opus.md:143:1. **(Preferred)** Make `walk_plan_for_address_only_deps` even shape-aware-er: for the LazyShape contract subset (ISREF in v1, future ISFORMULA-class lazy fns), skip volatile detection too. Add a sibling `walk_plan_for_lazy_shape_args` that NEVER recurses; or add a per-name policy:
quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-17-rt-step-3-opus.md:211:**Severity rationale:** HIGH because (a) the plan checklist explicitly enumerated this coverage class; (b) the no-eval guarantee is the SINGLE most important contract for `ArgContract::LazyShape` (the design's HIGH-B closure); (c) the regression risk is high — a future materializer refactor that "for consistency" applies eager-eval to LazyShape args would silently break the contract; (d) the current `isref_of_divide_by_zero_returns_false_without_eval` test only catches the case where eval would surface an error — it does NOT catch the case where eval succeeds but writes to the cache or fires side effects. This is the same pattern as Step 1's HIGH-O-1 (doc-promised invariant test missing).
quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-17-rt-step-3-opus.md:256:### MEDIUM-S3-O-1 — `step_2_reference_aware_names_registered_in_reference_tier` disjointness check missing `lookup_context_aware`. The test pinpoints ISREF / ISFORMULA must NOT appear in scalar / range-aware / unified tables, but skips the context-aware tier. A future typo registering ISREF as `register_context_aware` would silently slip through.
quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-17-rt-step-3-opus.md:311:1. **Semantic divergence.** Under the design's pseudo-code, `RefArg::Error(_)` would fall through `_ => Value::Error(ErrorValue::NA)` (arity error). The impl returns `Value::Boolean(false)`. These are different user-visible results. Even though the impl path is "unreachable under LazyShape contract", **someone might invoke `isref()` directly from a future test or extension**, and the behavior would silently differ from spec.
quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-17-rt-step-3-opus.md:315:Similarly for ISFORMULA: design says `[_] => Value::Error(ErrorValue::NA)` (arity error). quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-17-w5-d-1-opus.md:94:**Impact:** Behavioral inconsistency with the port source (IronCalc) **on the most-used arg type** (Boolean in numeric position). When IronCalc fixtures are eventually built to cross-check NORM.* — which is the natural next step for Wave 3 cohort-wide regression testing — they will diverge silently OR force re-port. Catching the divergence in documentation NOW means the future fixture-author knows where to expect deltas.
quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-17-w5-d-1-opus.md:183:**Recommendation:** soften the claim to: "the underlying distribution math reduces to identical `statrs::Normal::{pdf,cdf,inverse_cdf}` calls for any pair of inputs that successfully coerce to the same f64 — coercion divergences (see HIGH-O-2) are the only behavioral delta." This is the truth and matches what a future maintainer needs to know.
quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-17-w5-d-1-opus.md:281:1. **Dead code is hidden complexity.** A future reader sees `match standard_normal() { Ok(d) => d, Err(e) => return Value::Error(e) }` and wonders under what circumstances `standard_normal()` can fail. The answer is "never in this codebase" — that fact should be visible.
quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-17-w5-d-1-opus.md:286:(a) **Document explicitly that this path is defensive / dead.** Add a comment above each `match normal_with(...)` saying: "Defensive: Normal::new can fail on NaN mean / Inf-NaN sd, both excluded by upstream sanitize_f64 + the sd > 0 check. The map_err is unreachable but kept to match IronCalc's structure and to fail loudly if a future refactor weakens the upstream guards."
quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-17-w5-d-1-opus.md:288:(b) **Replace with `.expect()`** to assert the invariant explicitly. `let dist = normal_with(mean, sd).expect("upstream sanitize_f64 + sd>0 check guarantees Normal::new succeeds");` makes the invariant load-bearing. If a future refactor breaks it, the panic surfaces in the test suite immediately rather than silently returning `#NUM!` for an unintended path.
quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-17-w5-d-1-opus.md:314:This is correct (Excel: NORM.INV(0, ...) → #NUM!; NORM.INV(1, ...) → #NUM!). But the comment in tests doesn't make explicit why we reject the closed-interval endpoints that statrs allows. The risk is: if a future refactor weakens our pre-check from `<=` / `>=` to `<` / `>` (allowing `p == 0.0` / `p == 1.0` through), the test would then call `dist.inverse_cdf(0.0)` which returns `-Infinity` (not panic actually — let me re-read). statrs's source `if !(0.0..=1.0).contains(&x)` → for `x = 0.0`, `0.0..=1.0` DOES contain 0.0, so no panic. Compute: `erfc_inv(0)` = `+inf`. `mean - (sd * sqrt(2) * inf)` = `-inf`. Then `finite_or_num(-inf) → #NUM!`. So weakening our pre-check to `<` / `>` would still produce `#NUM!` from the finite-check at the end — but for the wrong reason (statrs returning `±inf` rather than us rejecting at the gate). The test would still pass with `Value::Error(ErrorValue::Num)`, but the failure mode would have shifted from "domain check" to "post-hoc Inf-filter."
quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-17-w5-d-1-opus.md:380:**Severity rationale:** MEDIUM. Not a bug, but the safety net `finite_or_num` exists specifically for this case and is never invoked by any test. Pinning the boundary tells future maintainers that the contract is "finite or #NUM!, no Inf leaks."
quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-17-w5-d-1-opus.md:388:**Detail:** We ported the first 4 functions from IronCalc's `normal.rs` (NORM.DIST, NORM.S.DIST, NORM.INV, NORM.S.INV) and left out the other 2 (CONFIDENCE.NORM, CONFIDENCE.T). The matrix doesn't track them as deferred. The audit prompt explicitly asks (Item 20) to verify they're tracked as future work.

A future statrs upgrade (0.19.0+) might gate, say, `GAMMA` or `BETA` behind a feature, and our `default-features = false` would silently strip it. The Cargo.toml comment claims the dep enables those fns; that promise has no test.

IronCalc uses `features = []` explicitly:

quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-13-w5-49-50-51-megaudit-sonnet.md:108:The implementation correctly uses `args[0]` as `x` and `args[1]` as `y` (Excel order: `ATAN2(x_num, y_num)`), and the actual call is `y.atan2(x)`. The doc title inverts the argument labels, which is confusing to anyone reading the signature. The function body, the inline comment at line 843, and the test `atan2_basic_quadrants` are all correct. This is a documentation-only error but could mislead a future maintainer.
quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-13-w5-49-50-51-megaudit-sonnet.md:152:However, as noted in the brief: Phase 3.3 sets `range.sheet = Some(_)` always during binding, so the `unwrap_or(fs)` fallback is currently unreachable. The future cross-sheet case (Phase 4.6) will work correctly if the binder sets `sheet: Some(target_sheet)` for cross-sheet refs. The one risk: if a future binder sets `sheet: None` for cross-sheet refs and relies on context, the supplemental builder would incorrectly scope G's to F's sheet. This is a latent risk, not a current bug.
